claims.text: Increasing the cooling rate during solidification will refine the lamellar microstructure of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Refining the lamellar microstructure by increased cooling rate will simultaneously improve yield strength and ductility.
Conventional cooling produces a coarser, less uniform lamellar structure.
Increasing the cooling rate will reduce lamellar spacing.
Increasing the cooling rate will enhance interphase-interface quality.
A finer lamellar structure creates a higher density of phase boundaries.
The increased density of phase boundaries impedes dislocation motion and thereby increases strength.
A finer lamellar structure distributes plastic strain more uniformly and thereby enhances ductility.
Compared with conventional cooling, increased cooling rate is expected to raise yield strength by approximately 15–25%.
Compared with conventional cooling, increased cooling rate is expected to produce a similar relative improvement in ductility.
Excessively high cooling rates may reduce the proposed benefits by forming nonequilibrium phases.
Excessively high cooling rates may reduce the proposed benefits by increasing residual stresses.
Analogous systems support the trend that microstructural refinement improves both strength and ductility.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on alloy composition and processing details.
The alloy composition should be held constant while cooling rate is varied.
